name: Stevie Wonder
hook: A Motown child star who won control of his own records at 21 and made his best-known albums inside TONTO, a synthesizer the size of a room.
blurb: Stevie Wonder was born in Saginaw, Michigan, on 13 May 1950 and has been blind since he was a baby. Motown's Tamla label signed him in 1961, at 11, and at 13 he became the youngest person ever to have a number one record in America, with the live 'Fingertips' (1963). At 21 he made Motown give him a new contract with a 14 per cent royalty, unusually high for the label, and control over his own music. With two producers, Malcolm Cecil and Robert Margouleff, he used their giant homemade synthesizer, TONTO, and from 1972 to 1976 he made a run of albums that musicians still study: 'Music of My Mind' and 'Talking Book' (both 1972), 'Innervisions' (1973) and 'Fulfillingness' First Finale' (1974), playing most of the instruments himself. 'Superstition' is one of the best-known records made on the Clavinet, an electric keyboard. 'Songs in the Key of Life' (1976) was the first album by an American artist to go straight in at number one on the Billboard chart. Its 'Pastime Paradise' became Coolio's 'Gangsta's Paradise' in 1995, and Kanye West has named 'Innervisions' and 'Songs in the Key of Life' as the albums he set out to compete with. Wonder's 1980 single 'Happy Birthday' was part of his campaign for Martin Luther King Jr.'s birthday to become a national holiday. He is still performing.

signatureTracks.title: Superstition
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The Clavinet riff, played by Wonder himself, and the drums too.

signatureTracks.title: Living for the City
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From 'Innervisions': a story about racism and a young man moving to New York, made with TONTO's builders and with Wonder playing almost every instrument.

signatureTracks.title: Pastime Paradise
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From 'Songs in the Key of Life', and the source of 'Gangsta's Paradise' nineteen years later.
